questions.question: If another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In the center of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when you start the engine?
questions.explanation: Always put your motorcycle in neutral before starting the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the dashboard that turns on when the engine is on and the transmission is in neutral.

questions.question: What does this traffic light mean?

options.text: The light will turn red soon.
The light will turn green soon.
Stop and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will turn red soon.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means the red light is coming. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required by law for all motorcycle riders in Georgia.

questions.question: Which surface is most likely to be slippery?
questions.explanation: Gravel roads have poor traction. Other slippery surfaces include wet or icy pavement, mud, lane markings, and metal plates or utility covers.

questions.question: How should your arms be positioned when holding the handlebars?
questions.explanation: Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you push on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen?
questions.explanation: Intersections have the most conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be extra careful when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar tough material for the best grip and protection.

questions.question: What should you do in high-risk areas?

options.text: Cover the clutch and both brakes to be ready to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brakes to be ready to stop quickly.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping centers, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brake levers so you can stop quickly if needed.

questions.question: How fast does the body break down alcohol?
questions.explanation: The body removes about one drink per hour on average. This varies by person. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: How can other drivers see you better while riding?
questions.explanation: Bright-colored clothing makes you easier to see. This works day or night.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger traffic gaps when you have a passenger.

questions.question: Jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely so wind can catch the fabric.
Fit snug so they don't flap in the wind.
Fit tight so you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snug so they don't flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly to prevent flapping, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, helmets are:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, you must wear a DOT-compliant helmet every time you ride a motorcycle.

questions.question: When carrying a load on your motorcycle, it should be:
questions.explanation: Secure loads low to keep your motorcycle balanced.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering heavy and difficult. This affects your balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet protects your head and neck. A leather or sturdy jacket also protects you. A sweatshirt does not provide the same protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black lettering tell you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is ahead.

questions.question: Riders under 21 are legally impaired at a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In Georgia, riders under 21 are legally impaired at 0.02 percent BAC. Never ride while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the following distance should:
questions.explanation: When towing a trailer, increase your following distance. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.
